answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may post bids, with deposits slashed when a challenge proves collusion or fabricated work. The protocol can raise the deposit as an identity’s delta of influence grows, so splitting control across many accounts does not dilute the stake needed to sway decisions. A Sybil attacker must buy and immobilize real capital for every persona, then risk losing it; a long voyage of cheap account creation becomes an expensive plume of exposed collateral.
